question: True or false: Stoic teaching held that a true sage would not turn pale in a storm at sea?
answer: False. Aulus Gellius watched a Stoic go white in a storm on a crossing to Brundisium and asked why. The philosopher produced a book of Epictetus: sudden terrors jolt even the wise before reason acts; the sage differs only in refusing to assent to them. The pallor was allowed; believing disaster had come was not.
move: Judge people by what they do after the first jolt, not by the jolt.
trap: Picturing the Stoic ideal as a man who feels nothing at all.
reference: Aulus Gellius, Attic Nights 19.1, trans. Rolfe, Loeb Classical Library, Harvard University Press, 1927
